newsitem.title: UK: Britain admits understating unemployment - papers.
newsitem.headline: Britain admits understating unemployment - papers.

text.p: British newspapers said on Wednesday the government had admitted in a report to the European Commission that its official unemployment figures understated the problem.

Several papers said Britain confessed to the failings of its own official statistics in measuring long-term unemployment in an application it made at the end of last year for funds from the European Union.

They said the application tried to make a case under the European Social Fund's "Objective Three" which sought to combat long-term unemployment and to help people "at risk of exclusion from the labour market".
The government was reported to have said its official figures, based on numbers of claimants for benefits, excluded many young people, women and older men from the tally.

"While a useful indicator of labour market trends, the claimant count is not fully adequate for the purposes of assessing the population which Objective 3 seeks to serve," the Mirror newspaper quoted the report as saying.

"There is implicit criticism of the exclusion from official figures of those seeking work who are not immediately available for work and others wanting to work who are 'discouraged'," the Financial Times said.
The opposition Labour Party immediately seized on the reports for further ammunition in its campaign for Britain's May 1 general election.
"These allegations point to systematic fiddling of job creation figures," deputy Labour leader John Prescott said in a statement issued late on Tuesday.
